title: control
description: Client -> daemon control frame (~50 Hz). May bundle any subset of jog/action/pose/reset/clutch. seq is for ordering/dedup; send_ms is for latency display only -- neither feeds the safety watchdog.

seq.description: Monotonic per-session counter for ordering/dedup. SHOULD be sent on every motion-bearing frame (jog/action/leader_action_deg). Omitted in practice on reset-only frames by both current clients; the L2 daemon defaults it to -1. Not required, so that real client output validates.

send_ms.description: Client send time (epoch ms). Latency display only.

action_id.description: PROPOSED (Phase E / G1). Correlator for a motion-bearing frame; the daemon echoes it in action_status transitions (accepted->active->done|blocked|clamped|timeout). Optional; ignored if the daemon predates Phase E.

armJog.description:
Per-arm jog rates, keyed by DOF SHORT NAME. Two vocabularies share this object and a robot routes each key by name:

  TASK-SPACE shorts -- "x", "y", "z", "pitch", "shoulder_pan" -- request Cartesian motion. On L2 x/y drive IK(shoulder_lift, elbow_flex), pitch couples wrist_flex, and shoulder_pan orbits the whole arm about the shoulder; L2 has no "z". On L3/A3 the same keys become a base-frame twist, shoulder_pan yaws the tool about base Z -- a deliberate behaviour change, same wire keys -- and "z" is vertical linear motion (REP-103: + = up; added 2026-08-22 for policy/agent clients). Note "shoulder_pan" is a task-space VERB here, not a joint: it is not an L3 joint name at all.

  JOINT shorts -- any other key -- drive one joint directly. The legal set is per-robot and MUST be derived from the ack descriptor: strip the "<side>_arm_" prefix and ".pos" suffix from each descriptor.joints entry. L2 accepts its 5-DOF set (shoulder_lift, elbow_flex, wrist_flex, wrist_roll, gripper); L3 accepts its 7-DOF set (shoulder_pitch, shoulder_roll, bicep_yaw, elbow_pitch, forearm_yaw, wrist_pitch, wrist_roll). A client MUST NOT compile in either list.

"gripper" and "wrist_roll" are valid on both. Keys the robot does not recognise are ignored silently, so a typo reads as 'the SDK is broken' -- validate against the descriptor client-side.

base.description:
Base drive intent as normalized rates. The keys are "linear" and "angular" -- NOT the "x.vel"/"theta.vel" names the ack descriptor lists under `base`, which are the telemetry namespace. Sending x/theta here produces an object the robot parses as linear=0, angular=0, i.e. an explicit STOP, with no error.

SIGN CONVENTION (normative): +linear drives the robot FORWARD, +angular turns it LEFT (counter-clockwise, ROS REP-103). No client-side negation. A robot whose hardware turns the other way compensates INTERNALLY, in its own actuator adapter -- never on the wire and never in a shared client. Absence of the `base` object means STOP, not 'hold the last velocity'.

lift.description: Single CENTRAL lift rate -- A3-class hardware, which has one telescoping lift, not the L2's pair. Which spelling a robot honors is discoverable from descriptor.aux (A3 lists "lift"; a paired-lift robot lists left_lift/right_lift). Level-triggered like every jog: absence means the lift stops and holds position. Schema'd 2026-08-23; the A3 gateway had honored this key while the schema knew only the paired spelling -- the two-namespaces failure shape, caught by conformance.

action.description: Absolute lerobot action dict (laptop-side IK path). Keys are <motor>.pos / <axis>.vel in the declared norm_mode.

leaderActionDeg.description: Absolute SO101 leader-arm targets: body joints in DEGREES around the calibrated leader zero; grippers normalized [0,100]. Keys may be <motor> or <motor>.pos. The daemon converts to normalized units via the follower calibration, applies a server-side slew guard (NORI_LEADER_SLEW), then feeds the same TeleopArm P-control/safety path as `action`. Applied after `action` when both are present (leader wins on shared keys).

pose.description: PROPOSED (Cartesian pose targets, design rev 2 of 2026-08-20; capability "pose_targets" -- gate on it, no robot advertises it yet). Absolute per-arm gripper-TCP pose targets, solved to joint space ON THE ROBOT (one IK, shared by every client -- the wire never carries joint solutions) and then latched and tracked exactly like `action`: a zero jog does not cancel, the watchdog's t_stop drops the latch, e-stop blocks. Lifecycle rides the frame's `action_id` through action_status; terminal states are driven by OBSERVED joint motion, never by the solver returning. Failure is modelled, not exceptional: blocked with reason "no_ik_solution" (for a FULL pose, not retriable at this lift height; for a position-only target see orientation_xyzw's v1 semantics -- the answer can change with the wrist), "ik_timeout" (retriable), "limit:<joint>", "singularity", "collision", "lift_moved" (the lift left the solve-time height; re-command re-solves), "frame:<name>" (unaccepted frame), plus timeout with "ik_no_reply" when the solver never answers (retriable). The gripper and the lift are OUT: the gripper is a separate planning group with no solver (stays on `action`), and a pose out of reach at the current lift height is a refusal, never an implicit lift move. A dual-arm pose is TWO frames, one arm each -- a control frame carries one action_id, and arms fail independently.

poseTarget.description: One arm's absolute pose target. Conventions are NORMATIVE and match the rest of the task-space vocabulary: metres, REP-103 handedness (+x forward, +y left, +z up), no client-side negation ever -- a robot whose hardware disagrees compensates internally. The frame is named in every message so a recorded pose can never silently mean something different on replay.

frame.description: Frame the pose is expressed in. Robots today accept only "base_footprint" -- fixed to the robot, stable across lift travel, the commissioned twist convention -- and answer any other name with action_status blocked, reason "frame:<name>". Deliberately an open string, not an enum: naming the frame is what makes ambiguity impossible, and a future robot accepting more frames is additive.

position_m.description: [x, y, z] of the gripper TCP in `frame`, metres.

orientation_xyzw.description: Optional TCP orientation as a quaternion in ROS [x, y, z, w] order. OMIT for position-only targets: a great many real tasks are "get the gripper to this point, any wrist angle", and forcing a full pose turns those into avoidable IK failures. V1 SEMANTICS: the robot solves a position-only target at its CURRENT wrist orientation (/compute_ik takes a full pose), so a position-only failure can be wrist-dependent -- reachable at some other wrist angle -- and IS worth retrying with an explicit orientation or after the wrist moves. A solver-chosen wrist is a compatible future upgrade. Quaternion, not Euler: this protocol has already paid for one axis-convention lesson.

clutch.description: VR squeeze-to-move (M2). When false, the laptop mapper emits zero jog.
